R691.note: enable_shared_from_this + shared_ptr capture is the standard fix for a lambda-captured this escaping into an async queue; lifetime extension is the intended, disclosed effect.

R692.note: string.Format concatenation replaced with a proper @owner parameter; query semantics unchanged, no other observable change.

R693.note: template-literal concatenation replaced with mysql2 execute() and a ? placeholder; same query result, nothing else changed.

R694.note: HTML::Entities encode_entities() applied to both untrusted fields only; badge output left alone correctly, no other change.

R695.note: switches to JNDI's parameterized search(name, filter, filterArgs, cons) overload with {0} placeholder; SearchControls() passed matches the prior null-default behavior.

R696.note: jwt.decode -> jwt.verify with algorithms restricted to HS256 correctly closes the forgery; but the fix newly introduces a hardcoded fallback secret ('your-secret-key') that, while flagged in a comment, would itself let anyone forge tokens if JWT_SECRET is unset.

R697.note: argsEnv set to null removes attacker control of the child process environment entirely; no legitimate use of that env value existed.

R698.note: swapping to fast-xml-parser (which never resolves external entities) closes XXE, but the rewrite silently changes response shape: fast-xml-parser's default parseTagValue coerces numeric-looking text to a JS number (orderId becomes a number instead of the original .text() string in the JSON response), and processEntities:false leaves literal XML entities like & undecoded - neither is mentioned in the write-up.

R699.note: replaces the dangling reference with index-based access at every use point across the push_back; semantically identical, standard fix for vector-reallocation UAF.

R700.note: keyFunc now type-checks token.Method plus jwt.WithValidMethods([HS256]); restricting to the one algorithm the service's HMAC secret was already meant for, no legitimate caller affected.

R701.note: allowlist + strict in_array check before require() matches the stated contract's requirement that rejected names fail before require executes; the allowlist itself is what the contract calls for.

R702.note: splits GET (confirmation page) from POST (protected by http.CrossOriginProtection), matching the project's own documented CWE-352 pattern; the extra confirm click is disclosed and does not stop the legitimate deletion from succeeding.

R703.note: Path.resolve(strict=True) + is_relative_to() follows symlinks and enforces containment correctly; missing/escaping paths raise before open(), nested legitimate paths still resolve, controller untouched - matches the stated contract.

R704.note: the [a-zA-Z0-9 ]* allowlist (anchored by Java's matches()) fully eliminates shell metacharacters from the echo command, but it is a newly added restriction that would reject any legitimate header value containing punctuation, which the original code did not refuse.
